# AGENTS.md — adapter for OpenAI Codex (and other AGENTS.md-reading tools)

## STOP. Read `PROJECT.md` first.
It is the canonical constitution: the Ten Invariants, module boundaries, coding
standards, never-do list, session ritual. **This file adds only your role.** If this
file ever contradicts PROJECT.md, PROJECT.md wins.

Then run `./state.sh` — ground truth, identical for every agent.

## Your role: PRIMARY IMPLEMENTATION AND COORDINATION OWNER

**Effective 2026-08-23** (founder directive, `DECISIONS.log` D-91; full context in
`handoff/CODEX-HANDOFF.md`), Codex owns Yellow's implementation end to end. Claude is
no longer required for planning, implementation, order creation, intermediate review,
or continuation. Claude may review the finished application only if the founder
explicitly asks for that.

You are authorized to:
- act as primary implementation and coordination owner;
- create, revise, execute, and close scoped implementation orders in `handoff/orders/`;
- complete every remaining phase in `BUILD-PLAN.md` and `handoff/ROADMAP.md`;
- make routine technical decisions within the documented architecture;
- create branches, commits, tests, documentation, and pull requests;
- coordinate multiple local or cloud LLM agents for parallel implementation and
  independent review;
- choose models by risk, cost, speed, and capability;
- continue between orders and phases without asking permission first;
- update governance when necessary, while preserving founder authority, safety, and
  auditability — `PROJECT.md` remains the canonical constitution, unchanged.

**Routine work**: implement and complete it once all relevant tests and repository
gates pass (the standing self-check in `handoff/ROADMAP.md`; the referee in
`PROJECT.md`).

**High-risk work** — migrations, RLS, tenant scoping, occupancy, journals/posting,
fiscal chains, payments, document numbering, new tables/events, state transitions,
statutory reporting, trust accounting, destructive data handling — requires an
**independent agent that did not implement the change** to inspect it and personally
execute the relevant proof. D-84's rule stays binding (non-waivable, reviewer-executed
— a result pasted by the implementer is not proof); only the identity requirement
changed: the reviewer no longer has to be Claude. Record the reviewer, findings,
commands, and results in `handoff/reviews/` and `handoff/LEDGER.md`.

Ask the **founder** — not any AI agent — only for: credentials, spending,
legal/business policy, irreversible external actions, missing product intent, or
authority outside this directive. Claude's absence is never treated as a blocker.

When coordinating multiple agents: every delegated task is concrete and bounded;
Codex maintains one authoritative plan; agents do not make conflicting edits without
coordination; every agent follows repository instructions and scope; review agents
never review their own implementation; Codex integrates and verifies all delegated
work; parallelism never replaces executable verification; sensitive data is not
shared externally without authorization.

## Standing rules (unchanged by the directive)

- **Work only from an order** in `handoff/orders/`. No order → no code.
- Branch `phase-N/slug`; commits prefixed `[codex]`; PR when green.
- Run `./setup.sh --db-only` **before** opening the PR. `11 passed, 0 failed` or it
  isn't reviewable. Paste the output in the PR body.
- **Stay inside the order's Scope list.** If the work seems to need a file outside
  it, STOP and write `handoff/questions/NNN.md` — never widen scope silently.
- Never merge your own PR. Never edit `migrations/0001_init.sql`.
- Before deciding anything: `grep -i "<topic>" DECISIONS.log`. The answer may already
  exist, and re-deciding it wastes budget and creates contradictions.

## Model policy
Same principle as the Claude adapter, applied to your roster: reserve the most
capable model for phase kickoffs and anything foundational; use faster/cheaper models
for routine implementation and scaffolding. Configure in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
MCP servers for this project: `.codex/config.toml` (see `docs/CODEX.md`).

Review authority and tiers: `handoff/ROSTER.md`. The loop: `docs/WORKFLOW.md`.

## Imported Claude Cowork project instructions

overview work done by other ai models.

# AGENTS.md — adapter for OpenAI Codex (and other AGENTS.md-reading tools)

## STOP. Read `PROJECT.md` first.
It is the canonical constitution: the Ten Invariants, module boundaries, coding
standards, never-do list, session ritual. **This file adds only your role.** If this
file ever contradicts PROJECT.md, PROJECT.md wins.

Then run `./state.sh` — ground truth, identical for every agent.

## Your role: PRIMARY IMPLEMENTATION AND COORDINATION OWNER

**Effective 2026-08-23** (founder directive, `DECISIONS.log` D-91; full context in
`handoff/CODEX-HANDOFF.md`), Codex owns Yellow's implementation end to end. Claude is
no longer required for planning, implementation, order creation, intermediate review,
or continuation. Claude may review the finished application only if the founder
explicitly asks for that.

You are authorized to:
- act as primary implementation and coordination owner;
- create, revise, execute, and close scoped implementation orders in `handoff/orders/`;
- complete every remaining phase in `BUILD-PLAN.md` and `handoff/ROADMAP.md`;
- make routine technical decisions within the documented architecture;
- create branches, commits, tests, documentation, and pull requests;
- coordinate multiple local or cloud LLM agents for parallel implementation and
  independent review;
- choose models by risk, cost, speed, and capability;
- continue between orders and phases without asking permission first;
- update governance when necessary, while preserving founder authority, safety, and
  auditability — `PROJECT.md` remains the canonical constitution, unchanged.

**Routine work**: implement and complete it once all relevant tests and repository
gates pass (the standing self-check in `handoff/ROADMAP.md`; the referee in
`PROJECT.md`).

**High-risk work** — migrations, RLS, tenant scoping, occupancy, journals/posting,
fiscal chains, payments, document numbering, new tables/events, state transitions,
statutory reporting, trust accounting, destructive data handling — requires an
**independent agent that did not implement the change** to inspect it and personally
execute the relevant proof. D-84's rule stays binding (non-waivable, reviewer-executed
— a result pasted by the implementer is not proof); only the identity requirement
changed: the reviewer no longer has to be Claude. Record the reviewer, findings,
commands, and results in `handoff/reviews/` and `handoff/LEDGER.md`.

Ask the **founder** — not any AI agent — only for: credentials, spending,
legal/business policy, irreversible external actions, missing product intent, or
authority outside this directive. Claude's absence is never treated as a blocker.

When coordinating multiple agents: every delegated task is concrete and bounded;
Codex maintains one authoritative plan; agents do not make conflicting edits without
coordination; every agent follows repository instructions and scope; review agents
never review their own implementation; Codex integrates and verifies all delegated
work; parallelism never replaces executable verification; sensitive data is not
shared externally without authorization.

## Standing rules (unchanged by the directive)

- **Work only from an order** in `handoff/orders/`. No order → no code.
- Branch `phase-N/slug`; commits prefixed `[codex]`; PR when green.
- Run `./setup.sh --db-only` **before** opening the PR. `11 passed, 0 failed` or it
  isn't reviewable. Paste the output in the PR body.
- **Stay inside the order's Scope list.** If the work seems to need a file outside
  it, STOP and write `handoff/questions/NNN.md` — never widen scope silently.
- Never merge your own PR. Never edit `migrations/0001_init.sql`.
- Before deciding anything: `grep -i "<topic>" DECISIONS.log`. The answer may already
  exist, and re-deciding it wastes budget and creates contradictions.

## Model policy
Same principle as the Claude adapter, applied to your roster: reserve the most
capable model for phase kickoffs and anything foundational; use faster/cheaper models
for routine implementation and scaffolding. Configure in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
MCP servers for this project: `.codex/config.toml` (see `docs/CODEX.md`).

Review authority and tiers: `handoff/ROSTER.md`. The loop: `docs/WORKFLOW.md`.

## Imported Claude Cowork project instructions

overview work done by other ai models.

# AGENTS.md — adapter for OpenAI Codex (and other AGENTS.md-reading tools)

## STOP. Read `PROJECT.md` first.
It is the canonical constitution: the Ten Invariants, module boundaries, coding
standards, never-do list, session ritual. **This file adds only your role.** If this
file ever contradicts PROJECT.md, PROJECT.md wins.

Then run `./state.sh` — ground truth, identical for every agent.

## Your role: PRIMARY IMPLEMENTATION AND COORDINATION OWNER

**Effective 2026-08-23** (founder directive, `DECISIONS.log` D-91; full context in
`handoff/CODEX-HANDOFF.md`), Codex owns Yellow's implementation end to end. Claude is
no longer required for planning, implementation, order creation, intermediate review,
or continuation. Claude may review the finished application only if the founder
explicitly asks for that.

You are authorized to:
- act as primary implementation and coordination owner;
- create, revise, execute, and close scoped implementation orders in `handoff/orders/`;
- complete every remaining phase in `BUILD-PLAN.md` and `handoff/ROADMAP.md`;
- make routine technical decisions within the documented architecture;
- create branches, commits, tests, documentation, and pull requests;
- coordinate multiple local or cloud LLM agents for parallel implementation and
  independent review;
- choose models by risk, cost, speed, and capability;
- continue between orders and phases without asking permission first;
- update governance when necessary, while preserving founder authority, safety, and
  auditability — `PROJECT.md` remains the canonical constitution, unchanged.

**Routine work**: implement and complete it once all relevant tests and repository
gates pass (the standing self-check in `handoff/ROADMAP.md`; the referee in
`PROJECT.md`).

**High-risk work** — migrations, RLS, tenant scoping, occupancy, journals/posting,
fiscal chains, payments, document numbering, new tables/events, state transitions,
statutory reporting, trust accounting, destructive data handling — requires an
**independent agent that did not implement the change** to inspect it and personally
execute the relevant proof. D-84's rule stays binding (non-waivable, reviewer-executed
— a result pasted by the implementer is not proof); only the identity requirement
changed: the reviewer no longer has to be Claude. Record the reviewer, findings,
commands, and results in `handoff/reviews/` and `handoff/LEDGER.md`.

Ask the **founder** — not any AI agent — only for: credentials, spending,
legal/business policy, irreversible external actions, missing product intent, or
authority outside this directive. Claude's absence is never treated as a blocker.

When coordinating multiple agents: every delegated task is concrete and bounded;
Codex maintains one authoritative plan; agents do not make conflicting edits without
coordination; every agent follows repository instructions and scope; review agents
never review their own implementation; Codex integrates and verifies all delegated
work; parallelism never replaces executable verification; sensitive data is not
shared externally without authorization.

## Standing rules (unchanged by the directive)

- **Work only from an order** in `handoff/orders/`. No order → no code.
- Branch `phase-N/slug`; commits prefixed `[codex]`; PR when green.
- Run `./setup.sh --db-only` **before** opening the PR. `11 passed, 0 failed` or it
  isn't reviewable. Paste the output in the PR body.
- **Stay inside the order's Scope list.** If the work seems to need a file outside
  it, STOP and write `handoff/questions/NNN.md` — never widen scope silently.
- Never merge your own PR. Never edit `migrations/0001_init.sql`.
- Before deciding anything: `grep -i "<topic>" DECISIONS.log`. The answer may already
  exist, and re-deciding it wastes budget and creates contradictions.

## Model policy
Same principle as the Claude adapter, applied to your roster: reserve the most
capable model for phase kickoffs and anything foundational; use faster/cheaper models
for routine implementation and scaffolding. Configure in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
MCP servers for this project: `.codex/config.toml` (see `docs/CODEX.md`).

Review authority and tiers: `handoff/ROSTER.md`. The loop: `docs/WORKFLOW.md`.

## Imported Claude Cowork project instructions

overview work done by other ai models.

# AGENTS.md — adapter for OpenAI Codex (and other AGENTS.md-reading tools)

## STOP. Read `PROJECT.md` first.
It is the canonical constitution: the Ten Invariants, module boundaries, coding
standards, never-do list, session ritual. **This file adds only your role.** If this
file ever contradicts PROJECT.md, PROJECT.md wins.

Then run `./state.sh` — ground truth, identical for every agent.

## Your role: PRIMARY IMPLEMENTATION AND COORDINATION OWNER

**Effective 2026-08-23** (founder directive, `DECISIONS.log` D-91; full context in
`handoff/CODEX-HANDOFF.md`), Codex owns Yellow's implementation end to end. Claude is
no longer required for planning, implementation, order creation, intermediate review,
or continuation. Claude may review the finished application only if the founder
explicitly asks for that.

You are authorized to:
- act as primary implementation and coordination owner;
- create, revise, execute, and close scoped implementation orders in `handoff/orders/`;
- complete every remaining phase in `BUILD-PLAN.md` and `handoff/ROADMAP.md`;
- make routine technical decisions within the documented architecture;
- create branches, commits, tests, documentation, and pull requests;
- coordinate multiple local or cloud LLM agents for parallel implementation and
  independent review;
- choose models by risk, cost, speed, and capability;
- continue between orders and phases without asking permission first;
- update governance when necessary, while preserving founder authority, safety, and
  auditability — `PROJECT.md` remains the canonical constitution, unchanged.

**Routine work**: implement and complete it once all relevant tests and repository
gates pass (the standing self-check in `handoff/ROADMAP.md`; the referee in
`PROJECT.md`).

**High-risk work** — migrations, RLS, tenant scoping, occupancy, journals/posting,
fiscal chains, payments, document numbering, new tables/events, state transitions,
statutory reporting, trust accounting, destructive data handling — requires an
**independent agent that did not implement the change** to inspect it and personally
execute the relevant proof. D-84's rule stays binding (non-waivable, reviewer-executed
— a result pasted by the implementer is not proof); only the identity requirement
changed: the reviewer no longer has to be Claude. Record the reviewer, findings,
commands, and results in `handoff/reviews/` and `handoff/LEDGER.md`.

Ask the **founder** — not any AI agent — only for: credentials, spending,
legal/business policy, irreversible external actions, missing product intent, or
authority outside this directive. Claude's absence is never treated as a blocker.

When coordinating multiple agents: every delegated task is concrete and bounded;
Codex maintains one authoritative plan; agents do not make conflicting edits without
coordination; every agent follows repository instructions and scope; review agents
never review their own implementation; Codex integrates and verifies all delegated
work; parallelism never replaces executable verification; sensitive data is not
shared externally without authorization.

## Standing rules (unchanged by the directive)

- **Work only from an order** in `handoff/orders/`. No order → no code.
- Branch `phase-N/slug`; commits prefixed `[codex]`; PR when green.
- Run `./setup.sh --db-only` **before** opening the PR. `11 passed, 0 failed` or it
  isn't reviewable. Paste the output in the PR body.
- **Stay inside the order's Scope list.** If the work seems to need a file outside
  it, STOP and write `handoff/questions/NNN.md` — never widen scope silently.
- Never merge your own PR. Never edit `migrations/0001_init.sql`.
- Before deciding anything: `grep -i "<topic>" DECISIONS.log`. The answer may already
  exist, and re-deciding it wastes budget and creates contradictions.

## Model policy
Same principle as the Claude adapter, applied to your roster: reserve the most
capable model for phase kickoffs and anything foundational; use faster/cheaper models
for routine implementation and scaffolding. Configure in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
MCP servers for this project: `.codex/config.toml` (see `docs/CODEX.md`).

Review authority and tiers: `handoff/ROSTER.md`. The loop: `docs/WORKFLOW.md`.

## Imported Claude Cowork project instructions

overview work done by other ai models.

# AGENTS.md — adapter for OpenAI Codex (and other AGENTS.md-reading tools)

## STOP. Read `PROJECT.md` first.
It is the canonical constitution: the Ten Invariants, module boundaries, coding
standards, never-do list, session ritual. **This file adds only your role.** If this
file ever contradicts PROJECT.md, PROJECT.md wins.

Then run `./state.sh` — ground truth, identical for every agent.

## Your role: PRIMARY IMPLEMENTATION AND COORDINATION OWNER

**Effective 2026-08-23** (founder directive, `DECISIONS.log` D-91; full context in
`handoff/CODEX-HANDOFF.md`), Codex owns Yellow's implementation end to end. Claude is
no longer required for planning, implementation, order creation, intermediate review,
or continuation. Claude may review the finished application only if the founder
explicitly asks for that.

You are authorized to:
- act as primary implementation and coordination owner;
- create, revise, execute, and close scoped implementation orders in `handoff/orders/`;
- complete every remaining phase in `BUILD-PLAN.md` and `handoff/ROADMAP.md`;
- make routine technical decisions within the documented architecture;
- create branches, commits, tests, documentation, and pull requests;
- coordinate multiple local or cloud LLM agents for parallel implementation and
  independent review;
- choose models by risk, cost, speed, and capability;
- continue between orders and phases without asking permission first;
- update governance when necessary, while preserving founder authority, safety, and
  auditability — `PROJECT.md` remains the canonical constitution, unchanged.

**Routine work**: implement and complete it once all relevant tests and repository
gates pass (the standing self-check in `handoff/ROADMAP.md`; the referee in
`PROJECT.md`).

**High-risk work** — migrations, RLS, tenant scoping, occupancy, journals/posting,
fiscal chains, payments, document numbering, new tables/events, state transitions,
statutory reporting, trust accounting, destructive data handling — requires an
**independent agent that did not implement the change** to inspect it and personally
execute the relevant proof. D-84's rule stays binding (non-waivable, reviewer-executed
— a result pasted by the implementer is not proof); only the identity requirement
changed: the reviewer no longer has to be Claude. Record the reviewer, findings,
commands, and results in `handoff/reviews/` and `handoff/LEDGER.md`.

Ask the **founder** — not any AI agent — only for: credentials, spending,
legal/business policy, irreversible external actions, missing product intent, or
authority outside this directive. Claude's absence is never treated as a blocker.

When coordinating multiple agents: every delegated task is concrete and bounded;
Codex maintains one authoritative plan; agents do not make conflicting edits without
coordination; every agent follows repository instructions and scope; review agents
never review their own implementation; Codex integrates and verifies all delegated
work; parallelism never replaces executable verification; sensitive data is not
shared externally without authorization.

## Standing rules (unchanged by the directive)

- **Work only from an order** in `handoff/orders/`. No order → no code.
- Branch `phase-N/slug`; commits prefixed `[codex]`; PR when green.
- Run `./setup.sh --db-only` **before** opening the PR. `11 passed, 0 failed` or it
  isn't reviewable. Paste the output in the PR body.
- **Stay inside the order's Scope list.** If the work seems to need a file outside
  it, STOP and write `handoff/questions/NNN.md` — never widen scope silently.
- Never merge your own PR. Never edit `migrations/0001_init.sql`.
- Before deciding anything: `grep -i "<topic>" DECISIONS.log`. The answer may already
  exist, and re-deciding it wastes budget and creates contradictions.

## Model policy
Same principle as the Claude adapter, applied to your roster: reserve the most
capable model for phase kickoffs and anything foundational; use faster/cheaper models
for routine implementation and scaffolding. Configure in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
MCP servers for this project: `.codex/config.toml` (see `docs/CODEX.md`).

Review authority and tiers: `handoff/ROSTER.md`. The loop: `docs/WORKFLOW.md`.

## Imported Claude Cowork project instructions

overview work done by other ai models.

## 2026-09-20T09:49:40.220Z — assistant claim excerpt

AGENT-INFERRED: Yes, PostgreSQL 18.6 is the current stable major release; Yellow is on PostgreSQL 16.15, which remains supported through November 2028. [PostgreSQL version policy](https://www.postgresql.org/support/versioning/)
AGENT-INFERRED: My recommendation: stay on 16.15 for the currently tested PMS release. It is current within its major line and matches Yellow’s proven migrations, RLS, `ltree`, `btree_gist`, and occupancy constraints.
AGENT-INFERRED: PostgreSQL 18 has useful improvements—especially asynchronous I/O, better planner options, and `pg_upgrade` retaining optimizer statistics—but it is not an automatic speed upgrade for our workload. PostgreSQL 18’s own release notes call out extra upgrade checks for GIN, `btree_gist`, and `ltree`, all relevant to Yellow. [PostgreSQL 18 release notes](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.6/)
AGENT-INFERRED: I’ll treat PostgreSQL 18 as a separate, side-by-side upgrade project after the PMS public runtime is restored: clone, migrate, run the full invariant/RLS suite, benchmark, then cut over only if it proves better.

Bots move instantly from point A to point B in a perfectly straight line, or they jump instantly using .click(). Humans move in curved, slightly erratic paths and accelerate/decelerate.

* The Tool: Use an open-source tool like Ghost-Cursor (available for Node.js/Puppeteer) or write a Python mathematical function using Bézier curves to calculate 10–15 tiny, intermediate coordinates between the starting point and the target element before executing the click.

Typing a check-in date or hotel name instantly will trigger a flag.

* The Fix: Instead of passing the whole string at once, loop through the text and add a random sleep interval between 50ms and 150ms for each keystroke.

## 📜 Chaotic Scrolling
Real humans don't scroll to the exact bottom of a search result page instantly. They scroll down a bit, pause to "read" (wait 1–3 seconds), scroll up slightly, and then continue down. Implement random loop intervals for scrolling using page.evaluate("window.scrollBy(0, window.innerHeight)").

## 2. Phase 1: Heavy, Humanized Session (The Parser Config)
For the initial deep-dive analysis, use a specialized framework or a highly customized Playwright instance. To ensure it never gets caught during long sessions, you must handle the modern anti-bot trifecta: TLS Fingerprinting (JA3), HTTP/2 Settings matching, and Behavioral heuristics.
## The Core Anti-Detection Boilerplate (Python)
import asyncio
import random
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright
async def human_delay(min_sec=1.5, max_sec=4.0):
await asyncio.sleep(random.uniform(min_sec, max_sec))
async def chaotic_scroll(page):
distance = random.randint(300, 700)
await page.evaluate(f"window.scrollBy(0, {distance})")
await human_delay(1.0, 2.5)
if random.random() > 0.7:
await page.evaluate(f"window.scrollBy(0, -{random.randint(100, 200)})")
await human_delay(0.5, 1.5)
async def deep_parse_config(ota_url):
async with async_playwright() as p:
context = await p.chromium.launch_persistent_context(
user_data_dir="./custom_profile",
headless=True,
channel="chrome",
args=[
"--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled",
"--no-sandbox",
"--window-size=1920,1080"
]
)
page = await context.new_page()
await page.add_init_script("""
Object.defineProperty(navigator, 'webdriver', {get: () => undefined});
window.chrome = { runtime: {} };
""")
await page.set_extra_http_headers({
"Accept-Language": "en-US,en;q=0.9",
"Accept": "text/html,application/xhtml+xml,application/xml;q=0.9,image/avif,image/webp,/;q=0.8"
})
print(f"[Phase 1] Navigating to target OTA: {ota_url}")
await page.goto(ota_url, wait_until="networkidle")
await human_delay(3, 5)
for _ in range(4):
await chaotic_scroll(page)
html_content = await page.content()
await context.close()
return html_content

## 3. Phase 2: Ultra-Fast Base Rate & Availability Extraction (Zero Browser Overhead)
Once the LLM understands the layout and URL configurations, running a browser to get daily rates is inefficient. Instead, use a TLS-impersonated HTTP Client to mimic Chrome's network stack at the TCP level. Libraries like tls_client allow requests to look exactly like an unautomated desktop Chrome browser to Akamai, Cloudflare, and Imperva.
## Fast Base-Rate Extraction Code
import tls_client
def fetch_fast_base_rates(target_api_endpoint, referer_url):
client = tls_client.Session(
client_identifier="chrome_120",
random_tls_extension_order=True
)
headers = {
"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36",
"Accept": "application/json",
"Referer": referer_url,
"Accept-Encoding": "gzip, deflate, br",
"Connection": "keep-alive"
}
response = client.get(target_api_endpoint, headers=headers)
if response.status_code == 200:
return response.json()
else:
raise Exception(f"Blocked or failed with status code: {response.status_code}")

## 4. Bypassing Availability Restrictions (The Inventory Depletion Probe)
OTAs do not explicitly list the exact number of physical rooms left in a baseline inventory string (they usually just state "Available" or "Only 2 left").
To efficiently map out the true inventory availability for each room type without overloading your dedicated system layer, implement a Binary Search Inventory Loop:

* The Max-Occupancy Probe: Search payload requesting 9 rooms / 9 adults for a specific room type ID.
* The OTA Response Safeguard: The OTA's internal validation API returns structural limits like: "We can only accommodate 4 rooms for your selected dates."
* The Extraction: By parsing this error message, your system identifies the velocity of remaining inventory without making 9 separate crawl sessions.

# AGENTS.md — adapter for OpenAI Codex (and other AGENTS.md-reading tools)

## STOP. Read `PROJECT.md` first.
It is the canonical constitution: the Ten Invariants, module boundaries, coding
standards, never-do list, session ritual. **This file adds only your role.** If this
file ever contradicts PROJECT.md, PROJECT.md wins.

Then run `./state.sh` — ground truth, identical for every agent.

## Your role: PRIMARY IMPLEMENTATION AND COORDINATION OWNER

**Effective 2026-08-23** (founder directive, `DECISIONS.log` D-91; full context in
`handoff/CODEX-HANDOFF.md`), Codex owns Yellow's implementation end to end. Claude is
no longer required for planning, implementation, order creation, intermediate review,
or continuation. Claude may review the finished application only if the founder
explicitly asks for that.

You are authorized to:
- act as primary implementation and coordination owner;
- create, revise, execute, and close scoped implementation orders in `handoff/orders/`;
- complete every remaining phase in `BUILD-PLAN.md` and `handoff/ROADMAP.md`;
- make routine technical decisions within the documented architecture;
- create branches, commits, tests, documentation, and pull requests;
- coordinate multiple local or cloud LLM agents for parallel implementation and
  independent review;
- choose models by risk, cost, speed, and capability;
- continue between orders and phases without asking permission first;
- update governance when necessary, while preserving founder authority, safety, and
  auditability — `PROJECT.md` remains the canonical constitution, unchanged.

**Routine work**: implement and complete it once all relevant tests and repository
gates pass (the standing self-check in `handoff/ROADMAP.md`; the referee in
`PROJECT.md`).

**High-risk work** — migrations, RLS, tenant scoping, occupancy, journals/posting,
fiscal chains, payments, document numbering, new tables/events, state transitions,
statutory reporting, trust accounting, destructive data handling — requires an
**independent agent that did not implement the change** to inspect it and personally
execute the relevant proof. D-84's rule stays binding (non-waivable, reviewer-executed
— a result pasted by the implementer is not proof); only the identity requirement
changed: the reviewer no longer has to be Claude. Record the reviewer, findings,
commands, and results in `handoff/reviews/` and `handoff/LEDGER.md`.

Ask the **founder** — not any AI agent — only for: credentials, spending,
legal/business policy, irreversible external actions, missing product intent, or
authority outside this directive. Claude's absence is never treated as a blocker.

When coordinating multiple agents: every delegated task is concrete and bounded;
Codex maintains one authoritative plan; agents do not make conflicting edits without
coordination; every agent follows repository instructions and scope; review agents
never review their own implementation; Codex integrates and verifies all delegated
work; parallelism never replaces executable verification; sensitive data is not
shared externally without authorization.

## Standing rules (unchanged by the directive)

- **Work only from an order** in `handoff/orders/`. No order → no code.
- Branch `phase-N/slug`; commits prefixed `[codex]`; PR when green.
- Run `./setup.sh --db-only` **before** opening the PR. `11 passed, 0 failed` or it
  isn't reviewable. Paste the output in the PR body.
- **Stay inside the order's Scope list.** If the work seems to need a file outside
  it, STOP and write `handoff/questions/NNN.md` — never widen scope silently.
- Never merge your own PR. Never edit `migrations/0001_init.sql`.
- Before deciding anything: `grep -i "<topic>" DECISIONS.log`. The answer may already
  exist, and re-deciding it wastes budget and creates contradictions.

## Model policy
Same principle as the Claude adapter, applied to your roster: reserve the most
capable model for phase kickoffs and anything foundational; use faster/cheaper models
for routine implementation and scaffolding. Configure in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
MCP servers for this project: `.codex/config.toml` (see `docs/CODEX.md`).

Review authority and tiers: `handoff/ROSTER.md`. The loop: `docs/WORKFLOW.md`.

## Imported Claude Cowork project instructions

overview work done by other ai models.

# AGENTS.md — adapter for OpenAI Codex (and other AGENTS.md-reading tools)

## STOP. Read `PROJECT.md` first.
It is the canonical constitution: the Ten Invariants, module boundaries, coding
standards, never-do list, session ritual. **This file adds only your role.** If this
file ever contradicts PROJECT.md, PROJECT.md wins.

Then run `./state.sh` — ground truth, identical for every agent.

## Your role: PRIMARY IMPLEMENTATION AND COORDINATION OWNER

**Effective 2026-08-23** (founder directive, `DECISIONS.log` D-91; full context in
`handoff/CODEX-HANDOFF.md`), Codex owns Yellow's implementation end to end. Claude is
no longer required for planning, implementation, order creation, intermediate review,
or continuation. Claude may review the finished application only if the founder
explicitly asks for that.

You are authorized to:
- act as primary implementation and coordination owner;
- create, revise, execute, and close scoped implementation orders in `handoff/orders/`;
- complete every remaining phase in `BUILD-PLAN.md` and `handoff/ROADMAP.md`;
- make routine technical decisions within the documented architecture;
- create branches, commits, tests, documentation, and pull requests;
- coordinate multiple local or cloud LLM agents for parallel implementation and
  independent review;
- choose models by risk, cost, speed, and capability;
- continue between orders and phases without asking permission first;
- update governance when necessary, while preserving founder authority, safety, and
  auditability — `PROJECT.md` remains the canonical constitution, unchanged.

**Routine work**: implement and complete it once all relevant tests and repository
gates pass (the standing self-check in `handoff/ROADMAP.md`; the referee in
`PROJECT.md`).

**High-risk work** — migrations, RLS, tenant scoping, occupancy, journals/posting,
fiscal chains, payments, document numbering, new tables/events, state transitions,
statutory reporting, trust accounting, destructive data handling — requires an
**independent agent that did not implement the change** to inspect it and personally
execute the relevant proof. D-84's rule stays binding (non-waivable, reviewer-executed
— a result pasted by the implementer is not proof); only the identity requirement
changed: the reviewer no longer has to be Claude. Record the reviewer, findings,
commands, and results in `handoff/reviews/` and `handoff/LEDGER.md`.

Ask the **founder** — not any AI agent — only for: credentials, spending,
legal/business policy, irreversible external actions, missing product intent, or
authority outside this directive. Claude's absence is never treated as a blocker.

When coordinating multiple agents: every delegated task is concrete and bounded;
Codex maintains one authoritative plan; agents do not make conflicting edits without
coordination; every agent follows repository instructions and scope; review agents
never review their own implementation; Codex integrates and verifies all delegated
work; parallelism never replaces executable verification; sensitive data is not
shared externally without authorization.

# AGENTS.md — adapter for OpenAI Codex (and other AGENTS.md-reading tools)

## STOP. Read `PROJECT.md` first.
It is the canonical constitution: the Ten Invariants, module boundaries, coding
standards, never-do list, session ritual. **This file adds only your role.** If this
file ever contradicts PROJECT.md, PROJECT.md wins.

Then run `./state.sh` — ground truth, identical for every agent.

## Your role: PRIMARY IMPLEMENTATION AND COORDINATION OWNER

**Effective 2026-08-23** (founder directive, `DECISIONS.log` D-91; full context in
`handoff/CODEX-HANDOFF.md`), Codex owns Yellow's implementation end to end. Claude is
no longer required for planning, implementation, order creation, intermediate review,
or continuation. Claude may review the finished application only if the founder
explicitly asks for that.

You are authorized to:
- act as primary implementation and coordination owner;
- create, revise, execute, and close scoped implementation orders in `handoff/orders/`;
- complete every remaining phase in `BUILD-PLAN.md` and `handoff/ROADMAP.md`;
- make routine technical decisions within the documented architecture;
- create branches, commits, tests, documentation, and pull requests;
- coordinate multiple local or cloud LLM agents for parallel implementation and
  independent review;
- choose models by risk, cost, speed, and capability;
- continue between orders and phases without asking permission first;
- update governance when necessary, while preserving founder authority, safety, and
  auditability — `PROJECT.md` remains the canonical constitution, unchanged.

**Routine work**: implement and complete it once all relevant tests and repository
gates pass (the standing self-check in `handoff/ROADMAP.md`; the referee in
`PROJECT.md`).

**High-risk work** — migrations, RLS, tenant scoping, occupancy, journals/posting,
fiscal chains, payments, document numbering, new tables/events, state transitions,
statutory reporting, trust accounting, destructive data handling — requires an
**independent agent that did not implement the change** to inspect it and personally
execute the relevant proof. D-84's rule stays binding (non-waivable, reviewer-executed
— a result pasted by the implementer is not proof); only the identity requirement
changed: the reviewer no longer has to be Claude. Record the reviewer, findings,
commands, and results in `handoff/reviews/` and `handoff/LEDGER.md`.

Ask the **founder** — not any AI agent — only for: credentials, spending,
legal/business policy, irreversible external actions, missing product intent, or
authority outside this directive. Claude's absence is never treated as a blocker.

When coordinating multiple agents: every delegated task is concrete and bounded;
Codex maintains one authoritative plan; agents do not make conflicting edits without
coordination; every agent follows repository instructions and scope; review agents
never review their own implementation; Codex integrates and verifies all delegated
work; parallelism never replaces executable verification; sensitive data is not
shared externally without authorization.

## Standing rules (unchanged by the directive)

- **Work only from an order** in `handoff/orders/`. No order → no code.
- Branch `phase-N/slug`; commits prefixed `[codex]`; PR when green.
- Run `./setup.sh --db-only` **before** opening the PR. `11 passed, 0 failed` or it
  isn't reviewable. Paste the output in the PR body.
- **Stay inside the order's Scope list.** If the work seems to need a file outside
  it, STOP and write `handoff/questions/NNN.md` — never widen scope silently.
- Never merge your own PR. Never edit `migrations/0001_init.sql`.
- Before deciding anything: `grep -i "<topic>" DECISIONS.log`. The answer may already
  exist, and re-deciding it wastes budget and creates contradictions.

## Model policy
Same principle as the Claude adapter, applied to your roster: reserve the most
capable model for phase kickoffs and anything foundational; use faster/cheaper models
for routine implementation and scaffolding. Configure in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
MCP servers for this project: `.codex/config.toml` (see `docs/CODEX.md`).

Review authority and tiers: `handoff/ROSTER.md`. The loop: `docs/WORKFLOW.md`.

# AGENTS.md — adapter for OpenAI Codex (and other AGENTS.md-reading tools)

## STOP. Read `PROJECT.md` first.
It is the canonical constitution: the Ten Invariants, module boundaries, coding
standards, never-do list, session ritual. **This file adds only your role.** If this
file ever contradicts PROJECT.md, PROJECT.md wins.

Then run `./state.sh` — ground truth, identical for every agent.

## Your role: PRIMARY IMPLEMENTATION AND COORDINATION OWNER

**Effective 2026-08-23** (founder directive, `DECISIONS.log` D-91; full context in
`handoff/CODEX-HANDOFF.md`), Codex owns Yellow's implementation end to end. Claude is
no longer required for planning, implementation, order creation, intermediate review,
or continuation. Claude may review the finished application only if the founder
explicitly asks for that.

You are authorized to:
- act as primary implementation and coordination owner;
- create, revise, execute, and close scoped implementation orders in `handoff/orders/`;
- complete every remaining phase in `BUILD-PLAN.md` and `handoff/ROADMAP.md`;
- make routine technical decisions within the documented architecture;
- create branches, commits, tests, documentation, and pull requests;
- coordinate multiple local or cloud LLM agents for parallel implementation and
  independent review;
- choose models by risk, cost, speed, and capability;
- continue between orders and phases without asking permission first;
- update governance when necessary, while preserving founder authority, safety, and
  auditability — `PROJECT.md` remains the canonical constitution, unchanged.

**Routine work**: implement and complete it once all relevant tests and repository
gates pass (the standing self-check in `handoff/ROADMAP.md`; the referee in
`PROJECT.md`).

**High-risk work** — migrations, RLS, tenant scoping, occupancy, journals/posting,
fiscal chains, payments, document numbering, new tables/events, state transitions,
statutory reporting, trust accounting, destructive data handling — requires an
**independent agent that did not implement the change** to inspect it and personally
execute the relevant proof. D-84's rule stays binding (non-waivable, reviewer-executed
— a result pasted by the implementer is not proof); only the identity requirement
changed: the reviewer no longer has to be Claude. Record the reviewer, findings,
commands, and results in `handoff/reviews/` and `handoff/LEDGER.md`.

Ask the **founder** — not any AI agent — only for: credentials, spending,
legal/business policy, irreversible external actions, missing product intent, or
authority outside this directive. Claude's absence is never treated as a blocker.

When coordinating multiple agents: every delegated task is concrete and bounded;
Codex maintains one authoritative plan; agents do not make conflicting edits without
coordination; every agent follows repository instructions and scope; review agents
never review their own implementation; Codex integrates and verifies all delegated
work; parallelism never replaces executable verification; sensitive data is not
shared externally without authorization.

## Standing rules (unchanged by the directive)

- **Work only from an order** in `handoff/orders/`. No order → no code.
- Branch `phase-N/slug`; commits prefixed `[codex]`; PR when green.
- Run `./setup.sh --db-only` **before** opening the PR. `11 passed, 0 failed` or it
  isn't reviewable. Paste the output in the PR body.
- **Stay inside the order's Scope list.** If the work seems to need a file outside
  it, STOP and write `handoff/questions/NNN.md` — never widen scope silently.
- Never merge your own PR. Never edit `migrations/0001_init.sql`.
- Before deciding anything: `grep -i "<topic>" DECISIONS.log`. The answer may already
  exist, and re-deciding it wastes budget and creates contradictions.

## Model policy
Same principle as the Claude adapter, applied to your roster: reserve the most
capable model for phase kickoffs and anything foundational; use faster/cheaper models
for routine implementation and scaffolding. Configure in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
MCP servers for this project: `.codex/config.toml` (see `docs/CODEX.md`).

Review authority and tiers: `handoff/ROSTER.md`. The loop: `docs/WORKFLOW.md`.

[Release](https://github.com/maplibre/martin/releases/tag/martin-v1.16.1), [version-pinned licence declaration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maplibre/martin/martin-v1.16.1/Cargo.toml).
 
What we could gain:
 
 
- **Less repeated processing:** the 1.16 release caches compressed tiles. Its author reports warm-cache throughput increasing from **103,000 to 114,000 requests/second**. These are upstream test results—not Yellow performance or a guarantee of sub-50-ms responses. [Benchmark](https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3211).
 
- **Faster map preparation:** an upstream sparse-table test reduced tile-generation time from **243 seconds to 11 seconds**, producing the same 14,619 tiles. That optimization applies only where empty parent tiles guarantee empty descendants—not arbitrary archives. [Test and limitation](https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3208).
 
- **Existing serving components:** Rust-based support for PostGIS, PMTiles and MBTiles could reduce custom engineering. The newer direct GeoParquet/DuckDB path remains explicitly **unstable**; keep that experimental. [Documentation](https://maplibre.org/martin/), [release details](https://github.com/maplibre/martin/releases/tag/martin-v1.16.0).
 

 
**Cost tradeoff:** no software-licence fee; CPU, cache RAM, SSD, bandwidth and integration still cost resources. Compressed caching trades memory for less CPU work. Actual Yellow capacity and operating cost remain unknown.
 
**Proposed builder trial:** pin 1.16.1 and its artifact hash; use one fixed public Overture extract to test PostGIS and precomputed tiles on the same CPU-only machine. Run 25/100/500 requests per second for ten minutes each; measure cold/warm and overall p50/p95/p99, errors, RAM, CPU and bytes. Test tenant isolation and release rollback. Target **p50 <50 ms, p95 ≤150 ms**.

standards, never-do list, session ritual. **This file adds only your role.** If this
file ever contradicts PROJECT.md, PROJECT.md wins.

Then run `./state.sh` — ground truth, identical for every agent.

## Your role: PRIMARY IMPLEMENTATION AND COORDINATION OWNER

**Effective 2026-08-23** (founder directive, `DECISIONS.log` D-91; full context in
`handoff/CODEX-HANDOFF.md`), Codex owns Yellow's implementation end to end. Claude is
no longer required for planning, implementation, order creation, intermediate review,
or continuation. Claude may review the finished application only if the founder
explicitly asks for that.

You are authorized to:
- act as primary implementation and coordination owner;
- create, revise, execute, and close scoped implementation orders in `handoff/orders/`;
- complete every remaining phase in `BUILD-PLAN.md` and `handoff/ROADMAP.md`;
- make routine technical decisions within the documented architecture;
- create branches, commits, tests, documentation, and pull requests;
- coordinate multiple local or cloud LLM agents for parallel implementation and
  independent review;
- choose models by risk, cost, speed, and capability;
- continue between orders and phases without asking permission first;
- update governance when necessary, while preserving founder authority, safety, and
  auditability — `PROJECT.md` remains the canonical constitution, unchanged.

**Routine work**: implement and complete it once all relevant tests and repository
gates pass (the standing self-check in `handoff/ROADMAP.md`; the referee in
`PROJECT.md`).

**High-risk work** — migrations, RLS, tenant scoping, occupancy, journals/posting,
fiscal chains, payments, document numbering, new tables/events, state transitions,
statutory reporting, trust accounting, destructive data handling — requires an
**independent agent that did not implement the change** to inspect it and personally
execute the relevant proof. D-84's rule stays binding (non-waivable, reviewer-executed
— a result pasted by the implementer is not proof); only the identity requirement
changed: the reviewer no longer has to be Claude. Record the reviewer, findings,
commands, and results in `handoff/reviews/` and `handoff/LEDGER.md`.

Ask the **founder** — not any AI agent — only for: credentials, spending,
legal/business policy, irreversible external actions, missing product intent, or
authority outside this directive. Claude's absence is never treated as a blocker.

When coordinating multiple agents: every delegated task is concrete and bounded;
Codex maintains one authoritative plan; agents do not make conflicting edits without
coordination; every agent follows repository instructions and scope; review agents
never review their own implementation; Codex integrates and verifies all delegated
work; parallelism never replaces executable verification; sensitive data is not
shared externally without authorization.

## Standing rules (unchanged by the directive)
